title: Machine-learning-assisted taxonomy identifies Limnognathia desmeti
summary: Learned analyses of transcriptomic data contributed to an integrative description of Limnognathia desmeti from the Crozet Islands, the second species described in Micrognathozoa. Phylogenomic and molecular evidence also contributed; machine learning alone did not establish the species. Greenland and Pyrenean populations were not definitively split. Limited specimen and population sampling constrains the result.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder and random-forest species delimitation
organization: University of Copenhagen; University of Barcelona; Natural History Museum, London

evidence.tested: Molecular analyses, microscopy and multiple delimitation approaches supported the formal description.
evidence.unknown: Broader geographic diversity and dispersal history remain uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: Variational autoencoder and random-forest species delimitation supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text species-delimitation Methods, taxonomic Results, date and affiliations; supplements not reviewed.
